description: Start a Mint asset-pack lifecycle from an explicit item plan. project_id is required when chat_id is absent; when both are supplied they must match. Use when the user wants a coherent set, kit, roster, lineup, or variations of model-ready assets. Supply prompt, asset_pack_type, style_guide, and 2-25 item prompts; item_count must match items when supplied. mode: "auto" is the default and proceeds through final generation where the runtime allows. Set mode: "review" only when the user explicitly asks to inspect, revise, select, or approve preview items first; then use revise_asset_pack_preview or approve_asset_pack_generation to continue. Show chatUrl as the Open in Mint link and keep assetId for follow-up calls. For code-project imports, follow nextSteps through wait_for_status and get_asset_artifact_manifest. Do not expose raw asset ids unless the user asks. If status is billing_required, generationStarted is false: use billing.userMessage as the core user response, explain the account entitlement or credit shortfall without promoting subscriptions, upgrades, or credit purchases, and present billing.chatUrl as a blocked request that can resume after billing is resolved. Do not call it a failed generation.

image_url.description: Public direct image URL. Simple share pages with public image metadata may also work.

riggable_character.description: Set when a humanoid character or character pack is intended for rigging/animation, or when the user asks for an A-pose or T-pose. Presence means empty hands and a strict front-facing camera are required.

hands.description: Required for rigging and animation: the character's hands must be empty with no held props.

pose.description: Animation-ready neutral pose. Use t_pose by default for riggable or animatable humanoid characters unless the user explicitly asks for an A-pose.

source_url.description: Source-page metadata only. Mint does not fetch this URL; use image_url for reference images.
